views.label: The event horizon

start.text: the cusp toward the pole $\theta = 0$, which runs on without end and is no part of the spacetime

legend: the event horizon $r = r_+$ at one moment, between $\theta = 0.2$ and $\pi - 0.2$

views.settings: $\ell = 1$, the unit of every length, $m = 18\ell/\sqrt{5}$, where the event horizon is $r_+ = \sqrt{5}\,\ell$, and the period of $\psi$ is $\mu = 2\pi$, the values of the figure of Gnecchi, Hristov, Klemm, Toldo, and Vaughan.
caption: The event horizon $r = r_+$ at one moment of $t$ ($r_+ = \sqrt{5}\,\ell$, $\mu = 2\pi$), drawn as a surface in flat space with every distance along it the metric distance. Its metric is $\Sigma\,d\theta^2/\sin^2\theta + (\ell^2 + r_+^2)^2\sin^4\theta\,d\psi^2/\Sigma$, so the circle of latitude $\theta$ has radius $6\ell\sin^2\theta/\sqrt{5 + \cos^2\theta}$, widest on the equator.

Toward each pole the horizon approaches the hyperbolic plane and runs out in a cusp to infinite distance, while its area stays finite, $2\mu(\ell^2 + r_+^2) = 24\pi\ell^2$ in all. The band drawn, $0.2 \le \theta \le \pi - 0.2$, holds $98\%$ of it, and the poles themselves are no part of the spacetime.
